title: feat: add model sorting controls
author: guus6457
pr_body_excerpt:
## What changed

- Adds model sorting for Newest, Title, Brand, and Price in both directions.
- Uses the shared UI package for a compact, right-aligned dropdown with background-only selection.
- Keeps search persistently visible, capped at 448px on desktop and fluid on narrow screens.
- Uses seven-day observed average generation cost for price ordering; free models sort at zero and unknown costs last.
- Persists search and sorting in the URL, including browser back/forward synchronization.

## Validation

- `npx biome check --write frontend/src/components/models/models.tsx`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx vitest run test/model-sort.test.ts test/model-categories.test.ts test/model-catalog.test.ts` (13 tests)
- Browser-checked the 448px desktop cap and 375px responsive layout without overflow.

gist.headline: The model shelf is sorted
gist.blurb: The model garden has acquired labels, a price tag, and the ability to put its newest blooms up front. Polli approves of finding things without excavating the whole compost heap.
gist.summary: The model catalog now supports URL-persisted ascending or descending sorting by Newest, Title, Brand, and seven-day observed average generation Price, alongside a persistently visible responsive search field.
gist.impact: Users can quickly find and compare models by name, provider, recency, or cost, with free models sorted at zero, unknown costs last, and search and sort choices preserved through links and browser back/forward navigation.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the model catalog as a cozy garden shelf of labeled seed packets and tiny potted code-plants, organized by name, brand, newest bloom, and price tags. Polli acts as the observant librarian-gardener, using a small sorting clipboard beside a retro terminal, while the visible search bar becomes a friendly magnifying glass.
